## What this letter says

You stayed in hospital on the Respiratory Ward. You had a chest infection (pneumonia). It was in the lower part of your right lung (right lower lobe). The letter calls it a community-acquired pneumonia.

Doctors used a score to judge how serious the chest infection was (CURB-65 score). Your score was 1.

In hospital, you had antibiotics into a vein (IV) for 1 day. Then you had amoxicillin tablets.

## What you need to do

1. Keep taking your amoxicillin tablets for 3 more days. This makes 5 days in total.
2. Have a new chest X-ray in 6 weeks. It will be at the Radiology Department. It checks that the infection has cleared.
3. You do not need to book the chest X-ray yourself. The hospital has already sent a request.

## Dates and medicines

**Dates**
- 5 October 2026: you went into hospital.
- 7 October 2026: you left hospital.
- 10 October 2026: your last dose of amoxicillin.
- In 6 weeks: new chest X-ray at the Radiology Department.

**Medicines**
- Amoxicillin, 500 milligrams, 3 times a day (TDS).
- Keep taking it (continue).
- You already had 2 days of antibiotics in hospital.
- Take tablets for 3 more days. This makes 5 days in total.
- Your last dose is on 10 October 2026.

## Questions to ask your doctor

- The X-ray is "in 6 weeks". Do the 6 weeks start from when I left hospital?
- How will I find out the date of my X-ray?
- Who will tell me the result of my X-ray?

## When to get urgent help

See your GP (family doctor) or call 111 if:
- you become more short of breath (SOB)
- your fever comes back
- you cough up blood

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
